Substitution of whey protein by carbohydrate and fat accelerated gastric emptying; while addition of carbohydrate and/or fat to whey protein did not alter gastric emptying or the gut hormone responses significantly.

the addition of carbohydrate to protein slowed gastric emptying and increased gut hormone and blood glucose responses, while the substitution of protein with carbohydrate did not alter these parameters, in healthy young men.
substitution of protein with carbohydrates and fats accelerates gastric emptying and reduces appetite.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the acute effects of protein, and substitution/addition of carbohydrate and fat, on gastric emptying, gut hormone responses, appetite, and subsequent food intake.
the effects of protein on gastric emptying, appetite and energy intake.
the effects of macronutrients on the gut and appetite.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
substitution of protein with carbohydrate or fat, and addition of carbohydrate or fat to protein, does not affect gastric empty rate, gut hormones or appetite in a significant way.
the addition of carbohydrates or fat to protein does not alter gastric emptying or appetite, but substitution of protein with carbohydrate or fat does.
the substitution, or addition, of carbohydrate or fat to protein does not affect gastric empty, blood glucose or appetite, or energy intake.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of carbohydrate to protein does not affect gastric empty rate and gut hormone responses, but the substitution of protein with carbohydrate does.
whey protein is a good source of protein to include in the diet for weight management.
the addition of carbohydrates to protein does not affect the gastric emptying rate, but substitution of protein by carbohydrates and fats does.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of protein on appetite are dependent on its content in the meal, with higher protein content leading to greater appetite suppression.
protein is the most potent macronutrient in terms of slowing gastric emptying and stimulating gut hormone release.
protein, carbohydrate, and fat all have different effects on appetite and gastric emptying.
